content: You mentioned that it is storing a huge password that you did not set. That implies to me that the account is OAUTH2 and the password was initially placed there by your email provider. Those special passwords cannot be transferred. You might try resetting the account by going to settings>privacy&security, clicking savedpasswords and then showpasswords and then highlighting the rows for the account and deleting them. That should let thunderbird prompt for password ,

content:
It is important to consider whether your font choice is for you, or for the recipient. In most cases, I recommend letting your recipient make that decision. Unless your priority is setting font for recipient, I encourage leaving the settings at settings>composition alone, That default is 'variable width' font and medium size font. That translates to "DO NOT send font style or font size.' Most users appreciate that.

Now for what you see, I suggest visiting settings>general and reviewing the font options there. That is where you control what YOU see. All the details are at https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/questions/1462509 Follow them carefully and you will end up with your choice of emails look when composed and when saved. If you have problems, let me know.

content:
Hello there Phil.matievic.


Okay , good you did cancel .

The message you are writing is short, but clear. It seems that the two systems are currently unable to communicate properly with each other through the server you are using.

There are a few things you can check to troubleshoot and restore the connection. In most cases, the issue is caused by your email provider's settings or the current server status.

When you use a provider like Gmail or Outlook, Thunderbird is essentially just 'knocking on the door'. This connection attempt can fail due to the following reasons: 1. Provider-side issues:Security changesServer outagesAccount locks

2. Thunderbird configuration issues:Saved passwords are outdated.Port or server settings are incorrect.

3. How to test and locate the problem:Try logging in via Webmail (your provider's website).

If it fails there: The problem lies entirely with your provider.If it works there: The problem is the connection between Thunderbird and the provider.

In this case, you most likely need to update your password or connection settings inside Thunderbird.
